title: The Viability Trap
author: Jens-Fabian Goetzmann
summary: Internal process decisions are business decisions with measurable impact on viability. Leaders often implement control-heavy processes without ROI analysis, yet require detailed business cases for customer features. Time allocation to internal restructuring rather than customer value creation directly increases costs and weakens business viability. Leaders must ask whether proposed internal processes make teams faster and thus increase viability, accepting slower processes only when compliance, risk mitigation, or strategic positioning justify deliberately accepting lower viability.
points: Every internal process decision is ultimately a business decision affecting product viability and financial sustainability
Organizations require detailed ROI for customer features but skip business cases for internal process changes that often slow operations
Processes designed primarily for control, gatekeeping, and reporting weakly support business viability despite good intentions
Higher costs from slower processes directly translate to worse business cases; opportunity costs are often even more significant
Leaders must consciously accept viability trade-offs only when compliance, risk, or strategy genuinely require it
quotes: Desirability is all about the value your product creates for customers and users. Viability centers on your business model. For every internal change you're considering, ask yourself: Will this improve our business viability, or will it actually make our viability worse?
I've seen companies spend countless hours debating internal process changes that ultimately make their operations slower.
Many companies require detailed ROI for new software features. Yet when it comes to internal process changes, they often skip this step entirely.
